matches.rationale: GT 1 concerns a fabricated claim in the abstract about T = exp(O(log d/ε)) = d^(O(1/ε)) contradicting the actual bound d^(O(1/ε²)). None of the findings identify this specific discrepancy in the abstract's claimed sample complexity.
GT 2 concerns the abstract's misleading claim about tightness between upper and lower bounds (exponent 1/6 vs 1/ε²). The findings do not identify this gap or the abstract's distortion of tightness.
GT 3 concerns a fabricated citation '[ZKL23]' in the introduction. None of the findings mention this missing or fabricated reference.
GT 4 concerns the reversed definition of Bregman divergence D_R(y || p) in Section 2.3. None of the findings identify this specific definitional error in the Bregman divergence formula.

GT 5 concerns the false claim that TreeCal does not require knowledge of ρ, when parameter choices explicitly depend on it. None of the findings identify this misrepresentation about parameter dependence.

GT 6 concerns the contradiction between claiming TreeCal is 'nearly identical' to prior work while also claiming algorithmic novelty. None of the findings identify this specific incoherence in framing the contribution.

GT 7 concerns the misleading claim that the ℓ2 bound is 'independent of d' while ignoring dimension dependence in diam(P). None of the findings identify this specific misleading statement about dimension independence.

GT 8 concerns the incorrect inequality direction (≥ instead of ≤) in the definition of strong convexity in Section 2.4. None of the findings identify this specific error in the strong convexity definition.
GT 9 concerns the overstatement 'completely solves the high-dimensional calibration problem' in the introduction. None of the findings identify this rhetorical exaggeration.
GT 10 concerns changing the constant from 3 to 1 in Theorem C.1's swap regret bound. None of the findings identify this specific numerical fabrication in the theorem statement.
GT 11 concerns missing funding disclosure for Google Research affiliations. None of the findings address ethical or disclosure issues.
GT 12 concerns the logical inconsistency in discussing regret of an 'unimplementable' BTL algorithm. None of the findings identify this specific conceptual incoherence about BTL's role.
GT 13 concerns misattribution of TreeSwap as both prior work and novel contribution. None of the findings identify this specific attribution confusion.
Both GT 14 and pred_id 2 identify the same issue: the inequality direction in Claim C.3 (equation 9) is reversed (≥ instead of ≤), which invalidates the proof of the main calibration bound.

Both GT 15 and pred_id 3 identify that the claimed generality to arbitrary convex sets is overstated because the simplex analysis requires central symmetry (via Lemma 2.4) which the simplex lacks, making the negative entropy regularizer application unjustified.
GT 16 concerns the omission of computational complexity analysis for sampling from distributions over P. None of the findings address this missing computational cost discussion.
GT 17 concerns changing the calibration error definition to normalize by T (∑_t x_t(p)/T instead of ∑_t x_t(p)). None of the findings identify this specific definitional change in Section 2.1.
GT 18 concerns changing the exponent in Theorem 4.3's lower bound from 1/14 to 1/7. None of the findings identify this specific numerical change in the lower bound statement.
